Subject: Capacity lattice and minimum GPU construct — proposal for ZenithAI

Hi Maya,

Great talking yesterday — appreciate the operational detail you shared about your inference burst patterns. Per our conversation, attached is a concise proposal that outlines a capacity-lattice approach (three-stage cluster growth) and the minimum GPU footprint we recommend to cover your production and peak testing windows while keeping unit cost predictable. Quick summary below: 

- Baseline (Week 0–4): 24 GPUs (min floor) to support steady traffic and integration testing.
- Growth lattice (Month 2): step to 48 GPUs (staggered over 4 weeks) triggered by usage thresholds.
- Peak/Surge (Month 3+): ability to burst to 96 GPUs via reserved burst pool and on-demand lanes.

Ramp cadence and triggers are included in the attached "zenith_mop.xlsx" (Operational Measures of Performance) and the proposal PDF. We also call out warm-up credits and a brief SLA addendum for 99th percentile latency during the initial 90-day ramp.

As next steps, can we lock a mutual action plan this week so finance can prepare the quote? If helpful I can pull in Marcus from Pricing to align on commitment tiers and offset credits.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: zenith_capacity_lattice_v1.pdf (proposal, 4 pages)
Attachment: zenith_mop.xlsx (workbook)

Thanks Vanessa — this looks useful and aligned with what we discussed. A few quick clarifying questions before we share with procurement: 

1) The 24 GPU "min floor" — does that include a hot-standby buffer or is that active capacity?
2) For the 48 GPU lattice trigger, how quickly can you guarantee activation (seconds/minutes)? We need to understand cold-start impacts on latency SLAs.
3) Can you outline the credit structure if we underutilize the minimum floor in month 1?

Also, the procurement team will ask for a sample DocuSign and an estimated monthly burn figure for the first 90 days (broken out by token compute vs. storage).

Best,
Maya Shah
Head of ML Platforms | ZenithAI

Maya — thanks for the quick read and great questions. Answers below at a high level; attached is a short FAQ page we've added to the proposal PDF.

1) Min floor detail: the 24 GPUs are active-serving capacity (not hot-standby). We recommend reserving an additional 4 GPU hot-standby pool for fast failover; that can be included in the quote as an optional add-on.

2) Activation latency for lattice step (24 -> 48): target cold activation under our Dedicated SLA is 3–5 minutes for pre-warmed images on the reserved pool; if you need sub-minute, we can provision a warmed lane (higher cost). The PDF notes tradeoffs for each option.

3) Underutilization credits: we propose a pro-rated credit for unused hours above a 60% utilization threshold during the first 30 days. The exact formula is in the MOP workbook and is flexible for negotiation.

Marcus and Neha — looping you in to confirm commitment tier options and whether we can accommodate a 30% ramp credit in the first billing cycle.

Cheers,
Vanessa

Attachment: zenith_capacity_lattice_v1_faq.pdf (1 page)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Maya Shah <maya@zenith.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity lattice and minimum GPU construct — proposal for ZenithAI

Maya / team — pricing side: we can support a 30% ramp credit in month 1 applied as a one-time billing credit against committed GPU hours (applies only to baseline floor). For utilization below 40% after month 1 we need to tie to a minimum monthly commitment to preserve lane allocation.

We suggest these concrete options for the term sheet: 
- Option A: 12-month commitment; 24 GPU min floor for months 1–3 with 30% ramp credit month 1; step to 48 GPUs month 4; 8% discount on list.
- Option B: 24-month commitment; 18 GPU guaranteed active floor with 4 GPU hot-standby; faster sub-minute warmed lane for burst; 15% discount on list.

I'll draft numbers and send an updated quote by EOD today.

-Marcus
Pricing Lead | Redwood Inference

Maya — a couple of engineering notes to set expectations operationally: 
- KV-cache priming: for model families with long-context traces we'll recommend an initial synthetic priming job during onboarding to reduce 99th percentile tail latency. That uses ~8 hours of a warmed 8-GPU lane; we can include that as a service.
- Canary cadence: two-week canary with automatic rollback triggers (error spike, latency regression).
- Observability: we'll provide per-route token-level latency and cost breakdowns in the Console; retention for traces beyond 90 days is an add-on.

If that looks good I'll add an implementation timeline to the quote.

Thanks,
Karthik
